_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Work you did in a local session on your own machine is now merged and live. It had been committed and pushed the whole time — it simply had no pull request, and it had branched before two others landed, so two sessions had rewritten the same search list without knowing about each other. Both versions are now one. Picking courses from that list has changed the way you asked for: ticking a row no longer does anything on its own, so the list stops jumping and losing your place; Enter applies everything you ticked and closes the box; Escape throws it away. Your ticks now survive typing more letters, because narrowing a search is how you hunt for the next thing to add. Underneath it we found something worse than the bug that was reported: pressing Enter could silently delete a course you had picked earlier and never touched. That is fixed, and guarded by a test that names the deleted course rather than just counting. All of it was checked in a real browser, not just in tests, because the complaint was about things moving on screen and tests cannot see that. Your v4 recording was also recovered and read end to end: six of its eight items had already shipped, and the frames showed that one thing we were about to build already works — so what is actually left is smaller than it looked.

items.text: Still the top of the queue, and still a sketch before a build. You asked for a CPL vs Course/Discipline toggle so exhibits and credit recommendations become the focus, and a show-articulations toggle revealing where articulations differ college to college — and called the two closely linked. The question that was open here is now answered by your own ruling: the toggle lights only what has a number and leaves everything else exactly as drawn, because only 1,490 of 49,896 points carry an articulation count and marking absence would claim something about the other 48,406 that the data cannot support. Next session brings you the picture.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. Say the word and it gets scoped.

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification was the pilot.

From your v4 recording: when you drag a course to a new home, nothing on the map says it moved. The confirmation sentence you asked for already exists — the frames show it along the bottom of the screen — so what is missing is narrower: the course's own mark never changes to show it is staged rather than saved. Two smaller things go with it: that sentence sits below the legend where your eye was not, and it says 'recorded below the map' while the panel it means is hidden in full-screen SkyView.

The legend's 'unified' is the only entry with no explanation — stand-alone course, noncredit and college course each carry one. You said a note on Unified would be fine, so that is the fix, in the style already there. Hovers explaining M-ID, C-ID and CCN go with it.

Build the two sketches Sam asked for before any code: the CPL vs Course/Discipline toggle and the show-articulations toggle, together, since he called them linked. The absence rule is already ruled — light only what carries a number, mark nothing else.

The course outline still has an empty layer waiting for credit-for-prior-learning: the MAP exhibits and military credit recommendations that could award each course. It is no longer blocked on a decision — that was answered — it is blocked on holding the text at all.

Decision packs still only exist for 5 of the 159 disciplines because they are baked into the page. Fetching them per discipline the way the course descriptions already are is the bottleneck behind several of the remaining asks.
